facts.value: Turn your passion for change into global impact. Learn about security, intelligence and diplomacy, as well as international trade, law and institutions from faculty experts and policy practitioners. Develop the analytic and communication skills and awareness of global systems to enact meaningful change in the public, nonprofit and private sectors.
You develop analytic skill sets and mastery of forward-thinking content areas.

You learn about national security, cybersecurity, AI and governance, intelligence, conflict processes, diplomacy, international trade, and both international organizations and countries across the globe.
This program allows students to obtain both a bachelor's and a master's degree in as little as five years.
Students typically receive approval to pursue the accelerated master's during the junior year of their bachelor's degree program.
ASU offers this program in an online format with multiple enrollment sessions throughout the year.
With more than 300 Global Education program opportunities available to them, international relations students can tailor their experience to their specific interests and skill sets.

Correctly apply one of the main theories of international relations, liberalism, to a global event or policy; Write about topics of international relations using clear and concise language; Apply social science research methods in research design.
Graduates pursue careers as foreign service officers, security analysts and policy analysts, and in other data-driven roles.

Graduates are prepared for positions in foreign service organizations, international agencies, legislative staff organizations, lobbying and advocacy groups, nonprofit organizations, multinational corporations, and government agencies.
foreign service, journalism, judicial administration, law, political analysis, political consulting, politics, public relations.
